context: Start from the existing instruction-target metadata and read-only audit, then compare the current skill materializer, lockfile, tracked snapshots, and generated target configuration. Define a manifest model for global and project-local files, including path expansion, precedence, ownership boundaries, redaction or opt-in rules, and portability. Implement capture, verify, drift reporting, and restore or export behavior with atomic writes and conflict checks. Add unit, contract, and integration coverage using temporary homes and projects; document the model, recovery guarantees, and rejected alternatives.
description: Build a high-quality local MVP for Claude, Codex, and Gemini Markdown instruction files. Capture and validate the exact global files ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, and ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md plus root-level project-local CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and GEMINI.md. Provide local snapshots, content and hash drift detection, and explicit conflict-safe restore. First define the small MVP contract, explicit six-file allowlist, local snapshot location, and source-of-truth rules. Implement exact content capture with SHA-256 metadata, validation and drift diagnostics, dry-run behavior, and atomic restore that refuses to overwrite changed files unless explicitly forced. Use temporary home and project fixtures for tests. This MVP intentionally excludes settings, hooks, permissions, trusted-folder state, nested or arbitrary rule files, remote sync, multi-agent translation, and cross-platform behavior until later requirements justify them. Keep the existing skills lock, skill materialization, and tracked skill snapshot behavior unchanged.

preserves.behavior: Credentials, tokens, and unrelated agent settings must not be captured by default.
Existing skill sync behavior, lockfile reproducibility, and tracked skill snapshots must remain compatible unless the new configuration model explicitly versions the change.
Existing user-authored content in global and project-local instruction files must not be silently overwritten or deleted.
